subject: East Coast service degradation — proposed failover + exec action / credit ask
messages:
From: Anya Patel <anya.patel@ridgeway.health>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: support@ridgeway.health
Date: 2025-11-17T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Re: sudden 503 / latency spike in east-us region — urgent

Hi Laura,

We started seeing a sustained increase in 503s and median p95 latency from ~120ms to 950ms across our east-coast traffic at 08:45 ET. Our health checks are failing intermittently and customers are reporting timeouts. Attaching a Grafana snapshot of error-rate and the kv-cache logs from our side.

Can we get an immediate routing change to move traffic to westus2 while you investigate? This is impacting checkout flows for a subset of customers. We also need to understand how Redwood will compensate for this downtime — please advise on credits and timeline.

— Anya
Anya Patel
CEO, Ridgeway Health
anya.patel@ridgeway.health

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Anya Patel <anya.patel@ridgeway.health>, Ridgeway Ops <support@ridgeway.health>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-17T09:22:00-05:00
Subject: Re: sudden 503 / latency spike in east-us region — urgent

Anya — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We’re elevating to a P0. I’ve put Dylan on a live troubleshooting bridge and asked David for a short-term routing option.

Immediate plan (short):
- Dylan to confirm whether this is a regional infra saturation vs model-level spike (bridge up, ETA 10m).
- We can divert customer routing from east-us to westus2 as a temporary step; that requires Ridgeway ops to accept a signed routing shift consent (we have a small change window).
- We’ll propose a one-time credit for the customer-facing impact; procurement can follow up via DocuSign so it’s processed quickly.

I’ll keep you updated on the bridge.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-17T09:33:00-05:00
Subject: Re: sudden 503 / latency spike in east-us region — urgent (bridge details)

Bridge: zoom.us/j/834-xxx (pin 7621) — joining now. Initial read: we’re seeing per-node CPU and KV cache eviction spikes on the eastus pool; token service latencies spike correlated with a burst of long context requests from a single client shard cluster.

Prelim diagnostics:
- Error signature: 502/503 amplify during high kvcache miss ratios (see attached kvcache-telemetry-11-17.log).
- Autoscaler did not add capacity due to a transient scheduling constraint at 08:47 ET.
- Westus2 pool has spare capacity and compatible model variants.

Recommended tactical actions (we can do immediately):
1) Initiate controlled failover for Ridgeway routed traffic: 20% -> 50% -> 100% over 30 minutes to westus2.
2) Temporarily pin Ridgeway to a slightly reduced max-context model variant to reduce kv-cache pressure while we fix upstream shard.
3) Trigger an autoscaler override to add nodes to eastus pool as a safety net.

I’ll coordinate the rollout if Laura approves.

— Dylan
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-17T10:05:00-05:00
Subject: Re: sudden 503 / latency spike in east-us region — routing & credits

Laura/Dylan — approved to run the controlled failover for Ridgeway pending their explicit consent (procurement/email). Kimberly, can you stand up the DocuSign credit template and a short POA for the routing consent? We should be explicit about rollback criteria and expected customer impact timeline.

Notes for the credit ask: I recommend an interim credit equal to 24 hours of steady-state token usage at average rate, with escalation to a larger credit if we see SLA miss confirmed after postmortem. Keep the DocuSign simple: acceptance of traffic steer and acceptance of the proposed one-time credit.

Also: request legal to preserve the eastus telemetry trace and mark as evidence for SLO review.

— David
VP, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

From: Anya Patel <anya.patel@ridgeway.health>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-17T11:07:00-05:00
Subject: Re: sudden 503 / latency spike in east-us region — routing consent

Laura, Dylan — we accept the controlled failover. Procurement/Legal are OK with the language; I’ve looped procurement@ridgeway.health. Please send the DocuSign and the routing consent doc. We need to minimize customer-visible errors — start at 20% and move to 100% as quickly as it’s safe.

Anya

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Anya Patel <anya.patel@ridgeway.health>, Ridgeway Ops <support@ridgeway.health>, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-17T15:45:00-05:00
Subject: Re: sudden 503 / latency spike in east-us region — routing completed and next steps

Anya — quick update from the bridge and actions taken:
- Controlled failover complete: traffic diverted 20%->50%->100% to westus2 between 11:10–11:30 ET. Post-diversion p95 latency returned to ~150ms and 503s dropped to <0.1%.
- Eastus autoscaler override added 6 nodes; we see KV cache warming; we will reserve telemetry for the postmortem.
- DocuSign for the one-time credit has been sent to procurement@ridgeway.health (link above). Kimberly attached the credit template and the routing consent doc.

Immediate next steps:
- Postmortem owner: David (will publish within 72 hours).
- Short-term mitigation: keep Ridgeway pinned to the reduced context model for 24 hours and monitor p95/KV miss.
- Customer comms: Laura to prepare executive summary for Anya and to include credit ETA and rollback criteria.

Thanks for the quick coordination — we’ll follow up with a clearer RCA and credit confirmation once legal signs off.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Attachments: ridgeway_grafana_snapshot_1117_0910.png; request-for-credit-v1.docx; kvcache-telemetry-11-17.log
